references.text: The continuation of the same passage that elaborates that God's word is near, in your mouth and in your heart, so that you can do it.
Paul quotes directly from Deuteronomy 30:11-14 to explain that righteousness by faith does not require impossible deeds, but that the word is near, in our mouth and in our heart.
The context that what has been revealed belongs to the people, and that God's commands are accessible for them to follow.
The psalmist's love for God's law and understanding that it gives wisdom, showing that the command is accessible and understandable.
The Lord's commands are pure and clear; they give light to the eyes and are not hidden or difficult to understand.
The Lord has made known to humanity what is good and what he requires, showing that God's will is not hidden.
The Lord has not spoken in secret, but has openly declared his will and his commands.
